authorship: Independent reviewer; authored from retained first-party source fixtures before inspecting correction diffs on 28/10/2026
scope: Fresh targeted natural-language questions; substantive answers and applicability limitations graded separately

cases.question: We lodged our annual return on 19 October 2026. Was the new question about a person carrying out the chief executive officer role already mandatory for that filing?
cases.subject: Annual-return CEO question commencement and pre-commencement filing
expected: The retained commencement notice states that the new annual-return requirements commence on 20 October 2026.
That commencement does not make the new CEO question applicable to a filing lodged on 19 October 2026.
The notice alone does not establish the complete requirements governing the earlier filing.
forbidden: The new CEO question already applied on 19 October 2026.
No officer particulars or other annual-return duties existed before 20 October 2026.

cases.question: For ACRA financial-statement filing, is meeting the small-company size limits enough to use Simplified XBRL if the company is publicly accountable?
cases.subject: Simplified XBRL small and non-publicly-accountable conditions
expected: The Simplified XBRL category requires the company to be both smaller and non-publicly accountable.
The smaller-company tests require both current-year revenue and total assets not to exceed S$500,000.
Meeting the size tests alone does not establish Simplified XBRL eligibility; applicable entity-specific filing categories still matter.
forbidden: Every company below the size thresholds may use Simplified XBRL.
Every publicly accountable company must use Full XBRL regardless of the separate bank or insurance filing categories.

cases.question: We transferred a payment to a non-resident on 14 October 2026. Does that transaction date change the general rule for when WHT must be filed and paid?
cases.subject: WHT filing deadline and transaction-date versus deemed-payment distinction
expected: The general filing and payment deadline is the 15th of the second month from the relevant date of payment.

For ordinary payments other than directors' fees, the relevant date is the earliest applicable contractual due date or invoice date in the absence of an agreement, account-credit date, or actual payment date.
If 14 October 2026 is the earliest relevant date, the general deadline is 15 December 2026; the bank-transfer date alone does not rule out an earlier deemed-payment date.
forbidden: An explicit October 2026 transaction date makes the general WHT rule unsupported.
The deadline is invariably determined only by the bank-transfer date.
The filing deadline is 15 November 2026.

cases.question: Our GST-registered business paid for staff medical examinations needed to renew their work permits. Does having a business reason make the GST deductible as input tax?
cases.subject: GST input tax restriction for medical examinations for work-permit renewal
expected: IRAS expressly identifies medical examinations for renewing employees' work permits as blocked medical-expense input tax under Regulation 26.
A business purpose or the employer arranging the examination does not by itself override that restriction.
forbidden: A valid tax invoice and business purpose automatically make this GST claimable.
All medical expenses are claimable whenever an employer is required to arrange them.

cases.question: A Singapore citizen on our payroll reaches age 65 in November 2026. For the CPF percentage age band, does the change start on the birthday itself or on the first day of the next month?
cases.subject: CPF age-band percentage change after the 65th birthday
expected: The new CPF age-group rates apply from the first day of the month after the employee's 65th birthday.
For a November birthday, the new band starts on 1 December 2026, rather than on the birthday itself.
An individual contribution amount would require the relevant wages and other payroll facts.
forbidden: The contribution percentage changes on the exact birthday.
A numerical employee or employer contribution amount can be established without wage facts.

cases.question: An employee obtained SPR status on 7 August 2025. Is the move into the second CPF contribution year on 7 August 2026, or at the start of September?
cases.subject: CPF second SPR contribution year and conversion-date fact role
expected: The first SPR year continues through the last day of the month of the first anniversary.
The second contribution year begins on 1 September 2026 for the stated conversion date.
The 2025 conversion date is an employee-status fact and does not itself request the 2025 contribution-rate table.
forbidden: The second year starts on 7 August 2026.
The presence of a 2025 conversion date makes the PR-year timing question an unsupported historical-rate request.

cases.question: For an Employment Act employee whose contract is ended by the employer, is the final-pay deadline the same seven-day deadline used when someone quits without serving notice?
cases.subject: Final salary employer termination versus resignation without notice
expected: Employer termination ordinarily requires final salary on the last day of employment.
If payment then is not possible, it is due within three working days from termination.
The seven-day rule belongs to resignation without serving the required notice, rather than the stated employer-termination category.
forbidden: Employer termination always permits payment within seven calendar days.
The employee is treated as resigning merely because the question compares the two situations.

cases.question: An Employment Act employee has Tuesday as a non-working day and Wednesday as the contractual rest day. What is the public-holiday entitlement if the holiday falls on Tuesday rather than Wednesday?
cases.subject: Public holiday on a non-working day versus contractual rest day
expected: A public holiday on a non-working day gives another day off or an extra day's salary at the gross rate of pay.
A public holiday on the rest day makes the following working day a paid public holiday.
The distinction follows the stated work schedule rather than assuming Saturday and Sunday.
forbidden: Both situations automatically move the holiday to Monday.
The compensation for the non-working-day holiday is only at the basic rate.
A rest day must be Sunday.

cases.question: Can a licensed investment manager use the MAS LFMC compliance toolkit as a complete checklist for the funds it manages, including duties outside the Securities and Futures Act?
cases.subject: LFMC toolkit manager-level scope and fund-level or non-SFA exclusions
expected: The toolkit is a non-exhaustive reference for common LFMC applications, notifications and submissions under the SFA.
It expressly excludes fund-level requirements and reporting obligations outside the SFA.
It cannot establish a complete checklist of the managed funds' obligations.
forbidden: The manager's toolkit exhaustively establishes all fund-level obligations.
All LFMC financial returns are obligations of every managed fund.
The general table establishes an exact QDC form or deadline.

cases.question: Notice SFA 04-N24 says it takes effect on 1 January 2027. Does its 21-day reporting rule already settle what a CMS licence holder had to do for misconduct first suspected in December 2026?
cases.subject: SFA04-N24 commencement and limits on earlier-period misconduct conclusions
expected: The retained notice expressly takes effect on 1 January 2027.
Its future rule must not be treated as the governing December 2026 reporting requirement merely because the notice was already published.
The complete earlier reporting duties require evidence for that earlier regime; this answer does not establish those duties.
forbidden: The new 21-day rule already governs the December 2026 incident.
There was no misconduct-reporting obligation before January 2027.
A refusal to apply the future rule proves complete historical-law coverage.
